# Kyoto Autumn Trip Outline

A 5-day Kyoto plan for 2 adults, centered on temples, food markets, and short transit hops. I’m assuming mid-range stays, a mix of taxis/subways/buses, and advance reservations for a few popular meals or temple-adjacent experiences.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary
| Day | Neighborhood Focus | Morning | Afternoon | Evening | Walking Load |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Oct 12 | Higashiyama | Kiyomizu-dera early visit; preserved lanes around Sannenzaka | Kodai-ji and Maruyama Park | Gion dinner walk; tea or dessert stop | Low to moderate |
| Oct 13 | Arashiyama | Bamboo Grove before crowds; Tenryu-ji | Okochi Sanso or river area; optional boat ride | Riverside dinner near Arashiyama station | Low |
| Oct 14 | Central Kyoto | Nishiki Market breakfast crawl | Kyoto Imperial Palace area or nearby temple pair | Pontocho alley dinner | Low |
| Oct 15 | Fushimi + Southern Kyoto | Fushimi Inari early shrine walk to a comfortable turnaround point | Fushimi sake district tasting and lunch | Return to central Kyoto; relaxed izakaya dinner | Low to moderate |
| Oct 16 | Northern Kyoto | Kinkaku-ji early; nearby Ryoan-ji if energy allows | Final souvenir stop and café lunch | Airport or departure transfer | Low |

## Map-Style Neighborhood Grouping
### 1) Eastern Kyoto: Temple Core

- Best for: Kiyomizu-dera, Kodai-ji, Gion, Maruyama Park

- Why it fits: dense cluster of iconic sights with short taxi rides between stops
- Pace: ideal for one temple-heavy day plus an easy evening food stroll

### 2) Western Kyoto: Arashiyama
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Best for: Bamboo Grove, Tenryu-ji, river views
- Why it fits: scenic, compact, and easy to cover without long walks
- Pace: strongest low-walking day in the itinerary

### 3) Central Kyoto: Markets and Old Streets
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
- Best for: Nishiki Market, Pontocho, nearby city temples
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/A_store_at_Nishiki_market%2C_Kyoto%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=Best for: Nishiki Market, Pontocho, nearby city temples, Kyoto, Japan
- Why it fits: food-first day with flexible pacing and short transfers
- Pace: good recovery day between temple-heavy outings

### 4) Southern Kyoto: Shrine and Sake Area
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
- Best for: Fushimi Inari, Fushimi sake district
- Why it fits: combines a major landmark with a tasting-friendly neighborhood
- Pace: manageable if you keep the shrine walk to a moderate segment

### 5) Northern Kyoto: Grand Finale
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/sun.svg
- Best for: Kinkaku-ji, Ryoan-ji, calm café stop
- Why it fits: iconic sights with a simple half-day structure
- Pace: clean closing day before departure

## Budget Breakdown for 2 Adults
| Category | Planned Amount | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Hotel, 4 nights | USD 880 | Mid-range central stay, easy transit access |
| Local transport | USD 180 | Subway, bus, and occasional taxi rides |
| Meals and snacks | USD 520 | Temple-area lunches, market food, dinner set meals |
| Temple/admission fees | USD 120 | Multiple paid entries, gardens, and small attractions |
| Sake tasting / special food | USD 120 | One tasting session plus a premium meal |
| Shopping / souvenirs | USD 180 | Tea, sweets, ceramics, small gifts |
| Buffer / flexibility | USD 200 | Weather, upgrades, or extra taxi rides |
| Total | **USD 2,200** | Excludes international flights |

## Budget Snapshot
- **Lodging:** 40%
- **Food:** 24%
- **Transport:** 8%
- **Admissions:** 5%
- **Experiences:** 5%
- **Shopping + buffer:** 18%
